chapters.title: The Friction
chapters.teaserText: A transfer should feel like a promise—not a gamble.
chapters.deepDiveHtml:
Before mobile-first challengers, international transfers passed through a patchwork of banks, wire services, storefront agents, and informal networks. For migrant workers, that meant stacked fees, exchange-rate markups, slow settlement, limited payout options, and almost no visibility.

The consequences were personal. These transfers often paid for food, rent, school, and medicine. The sender was usually an immigrant earning in a wealthier country while a household elsewhere depended on the transfer as a lifeline—not discretionary spending.

Remitly’s founding story begins with Matt Oppenheimer seeing that imbalance while working in Nairobi: sending support home could feel confusing, expensive, and unreliable enough to seem exploitative.

chapters.title: The Founder(s)
chapters.teaserText: One observed problem became a three-founder mission.
chapters.deepDiveHtml:
Remitly was founded in Seattle in May 2011 by Matt Oppenheimer, Josh Hug, and Shivaas Gulati. The company began as BeamIt Mobile and adopted the Remitly name in August 2012.

Oppenheimer’s time leading mobile and internet banking initiatives for Barclays in Nairobi supplied the problem insight. Gulati brought early engineering leadership. Hug added consumer-product experience from Shelfari and a personal understanding of cross-border family connections.

The team passed through Highway 12 Ventures in Idaho and Techstars Seattle. Their earliest concept was a comparison engine for remittance providers; controlling the full customer experience required becoming a direct money transmitter instead. The enduring accelerator lesson was to stay attached to the problem, not the first proposed solution.

chapters.title: The Business Model
chapters.teaserText: Two small slices of every transfer built a large network.
chapters.deepDiveHtml:
Remitly primarily earns transaction fees and an FX spread. Fees vary by corridor, funding method, delivery speed, and payout choice. The FX spread is the difference between wholesale currency access and the retail rate shown to a customer.

The sender generally pays both economics, while the recipient receives the displayed converted amount without a separate Remitly fee. Newer products broaden the model through Remitly One membership, Flex credit, Wallet, and Remitly Business.

For case-study context, the historical revenue mix is often described illustratively as roughly 40% transaction fees and 60% FX spread. This is a teaching approximation, not current segment reporting.

Reported revenue grew from about $944 million in 2023 to roughly $1.26 billion in 2024 and around $1.6 billion in 2025. Q1 2026 revenue was reported at $452.8 million. The company reached its first GAAP-profitable quarter since the IPO in Q1 2025, while gross margin remained near 60%.

chapters.title: Geography & Scale
chapters.teaserText: A Seattle pin became a six-continent payments network.
chapters.deepDiveHtml:
Remitly started in Seattle in 2011 and grew from a handful of send corridors into a global cross-border network. It listed on Nasdaq under RELY on September 23, 2021.

By the 2025–2026 period, company materials described more than nine million active customers, more than 175 countries reached, and more than 100 currencies supported across bank deposit, cash pickup, mobile wallet, home delivery, and card payout channels.

Recent expansion included direct licensing in the UAE and extending Remitly Business beyond the United States into the United Kingdom and Canada.

chapters.title: Status Today
chapters.teaserText: The heartbeat changed rhythm; it did not slow down.
chapters.deepDiveHtml:
Remitly remains an operating, publicly traded company on Nasdaq under RELY. In February 2026, Sebastian J. Gunningham became CEO and co-founder Matt Oppenheimer moved to chairman after nearly fifteen years leading the business.

The transition marks a familiar public-company inflection: the founder-led remittance challenger is becoming a multi-product financial platform. Under the new leadership structure, the company reported record Q1 2026 revenue of $452.8 million alongside continued profitability.

Remitly is also diversifying beyond its original transfer product through Business, One, Flex, Wallet, and audience-building partnerships. Its strategic question is no longer simply whether digital remittances work, but whether the company can serve more of immigrant households’ financial lives.

Market data changes continuously. The market-cap figure shown here is an editorial mid-2026 range and should be verified against current filings or market data before academic submission.

founders.name: Matt Oppenheimer
founders.background: Dartmouth psychology graduate, Harvard MBA, and former Barclays mobile-banking leader in Nairobi.
founders.personalConnection: Observed how expensive and uncertain it was for people to support family across borders.

founders.name: Josh Hug
founders.background: Co-founded Shelfari, acquired by Amazon in 2008, and first advised the team through Techstars.
founders.personalConnection: Had family abroad and understood the everyday difficulty of moving money internationally.

founders.name: Shivaas Gulati
founders.background: Connected with Oppenheimer before Techstars and helped turn the concept into a mobile-first product.
founders.personalConnection: Built the technology needed to replace an opaque offline experience with a trackable digital one.
